newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Hoogovens, UGB seal 4.25 billion Bfr steel alliance.
newsitem.headline: Hoogovens, UGB seal 4.25 billion Bfr steel alliance.

text.p: Dutch steel maker Hoogovens and smaller, privately-owned Belgian steel firm Usines Gustave Boel (UGB) said on Friday they had signed a long-awaited 50/50 joint venture.
Under the terms of the link-up 4.25 billion Belgian francs ($121.8 million) in fresh funds will be injected into UGB, of which Hoogovens will pay 2.25 billion francs.

The steel sector investment company of Belgium's Walloon region, where IGB is located, will invest 500 million francs and UGB's present shareholders, mainly the Boel family, will pay the remainder. The new funds will come in the form of cash and subordinated loans.
The 50/50 joint venture to be formed by Hoogovens and the present shareholders of UGB will act as a holding company, owning 100 percent of UGB and of UGB subsidiary Fabrique de Fer de Maubeuge.

Hoogovens already supplies semi-products to UGB's rolling mills. "The market positions of UGB and Hoogovens can thus be optimised to the benefit of their customers," the companies said in a statement.
The definitive closure of the deal was pending approval by the European commission.
"There will be two types of investment, one in personnel and one in the installations," Aad van der Velden, a member of Hoogoven's executive commitee, told a news conference.
"We will invest in organisation, the personnel and in training, to modernise it," he said.

There would also be investment in the technology of UGB's cold and hot rolling mills at the company's La Louviere site, south west of Brussels, and the addition of a cost-cutting coal and oxygen injection option to the electrical arc furnace.
As a result of the restructuring the number of workers at La Louviere is being cut to 1,300 from just over 2,000.
The new Hoogovens-UGB alliance will have annual capacity of 500,000 tonnes of steel a year from the electrical furnace.

For long and flat products capacity will include 950,000 to one million tonnes of hot and cold laminated coils, 200,000 tonnes of rolling semi-finished products on contract, and 250,000 tonnes of steel wire.
Flat galvanised and painted steel capacity will be 300,000 tonnes of coils, sheets and profiles.
